best_idea: A client estimates the server's turn position from a 250 ms broadcast plus half the ping, extrapolates it by sample age, and nudges its clock rate by the error divided by 64, clamped to 1 ms, dropping the sample after 750 ms.
decision_why: Take the client clock nudge (rate-only, clamped, staleness-guarded) for input timing and hit-window display, but reject the lockstep wait: the server is authoritative and must never wait on a client.
acceptance: A client test with a synthetic 80 ms ping and 5 ms clock error converges to within 2 ms in under 2 s, changes its rate by at most 1 ms per recompute, and reverts to zero nudge when no sample arrives for 750 ms; no server result depends on a client nudge.
